record.title: Paper reports pre-action memory signals and selective evidence retrieval for long-horizon agents
record.summary: The PaMER paper studies whether an agent’s hidden state contains signals that predict when to compress context or retrieve older evidence. It proposes state-guided compression and selective raw-evidence retrieval. On the authors’ 260-task WorkBuddyBench evaluation with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, PaMER reduced mean total input/output tokens by 73.2% while mean task reward changed from 69.9 to 69.4; PaMER+ reduced tokens by 71.7% and raised mean reward to 71.6. These results are author-reported and specific to the benchmark, harness and model configuration.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that hidden representations predict compression and recall decisions better than observable length/turn metadata on their decision corpus (mean AUROC 0.831 vs 0.751 for compression and 0.765 vs 0.552 for recall).

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the 260-task WorkBuddyBench evaluation with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, PaMER reduced mean total input/output tokens by 73.2% with mean reward 69.4 vs 69.9 for the base; PaMER+ reduced tokens by 71.7% and reported mean reward 71.6.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On a fixed 40-task comparison, the paper reports PaMER and PaMER+ using about 52.4% and 48.1% fewer tokens respectively than the base while achieving slightly higher average reward in that test set.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The token measure includes input and output tokens across the main agent and auxiliary memory calls, but does not establish total latency, storage, external-tool costs or cost under other inference pricing and hardware regimes.

evidence_gaps.description: Reproduce on WorkBuddyBench using pinned model and harness versions; report total wall time, memory storage, tool calls and cost as well as tokens.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported token-quality tradeoff generalizes, hidden-state-guided memory control could make long-horizon agents materially cheaper to run without relying only on fixed-window or periodic-summary heuristics. Importance reflects the potential systems consequence; the benchmark results remain unconfirmed.
limitations: Results come from one paper-reported benchmark and specific model/harness settings.
The full benchmark and fixed Pilot40 results are distinct evaluation sets; token reductions do not alone establish total operating-cost reductions.
No independent implementation or reproduction was checked.
brief.summary: The PaMER paper studies whether an agent’s hidden state contains signals that predict when to compress context or retrieve older evidence. It proposes state-guided compression and selective raw-evidence retrieval. On the authors’ 260-task WorkBuddyBench evaluation with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, PaMER reduced mean total input/output tokens by 73.2% while mean task reward changed from 69.9 to 69.4; PaMER+ reduced tokens by 71.7% and raised mean reward to 71.6. These results are author-reported and specific to the benchmark, harness and model configuration.

technical.claimed_result: For DeepSeek-V4-Flash on the full 260-task set, the authors report mean reward 69.9 and 2.69M tokens for the base, 69.4 and 0.72M for PaMER, and 71.6 and 0.76M for PaMER+. Table 4 reports the fixed 40-task comparison with 52.4% and 48.1% token reductions for PaMER and PaMER+.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper defines the memory-control and evidence-retrieval methods and reports benchmark results; no independent reproduction was performed.
technical.mechanism: PaMER reads hidden-state signals associated with memory-control decisions, applies state-guided context compression and retrieves selected raw historical evidence. PaMER+ adds step-level evidence selection.
technical.regime: The paper’s WorkBuddyBench contains 260 tasks across Code, Office, Security and Web. The full-benchmark comparison uses DeepSeek-V4-Flash; a separate method comparison uses the same fixed Pilot40 tasks. The memory-decision corpus is separate from the benchmark tasks.
technical.strongest_baseline: The same DeepSeek-V4-Flash base agent and fixed context-management baselines on WorkBuddyBench. Pilot40 is a fixed 40-task subset and should be treated separately from the full 260-task result.

brief.title: Paper reports pre-action memory signals and selective evidence retrieval for long-horizon agents
brief.why_it_matters: The result isolates memory control as a distinct systems problem: selecting when to compress and which prior evidence to restore may reduce context load while retaining task quality in the tested agent regime.
